transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-11-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42 mins | Attendees: Carlos Mendez, Priya Reddy, Ethan Zhao (Redwood) ; Dr. Laura Kim, Marcus Allen, Tara Singh, Jamal Ortiz (Suncrest)

Summary: kickoff, roles, timeline, VPC/SSO/KMS, sample workloads, next steps.

00:00 Carlos: Hey everyone thanks for joining on time, I'll hand it over to Priya to run through the agenda, but quick intro - I'm Carlos, account exec on the Redwood side.
00:14 Priya: Yeah hi all, Priya Reddy CSM, we'll take about 40 minutes, go over the onboarding plan, who does what, and then technical deep-dive with Ethan for network and security.
00:28 Dr. Laura: Thanks, we got Marcus and Tara and Jamal on; hoping to get the integration started ASAP, timeline is Jan production target.
00:42 Marcus: Yeah Jan would be ideal, subject to security review and some bench testing.
00:55 Priya: Totally, we'll map the milestones to that timeline. Agenda: 1) roles and contacts, 2) security and compliance checklist, 3) infra: VPC peering, private deployment options, 4) dev/staging plan, 5) next steps.
01:12 Tara: Sounds good. Quick question on the private deployment, we talked about a VPC option during eval, do we need dedicated GPUs for initial pilot?
01:28 Ethan: So for pilot you don't necessarily need Dedicated, you can run on hosted with private networking, but if you want consistent throughput and lower jitter we recommend Redwood Dedicated and reserved capacity. For small pilot, we can do staged approach: hosted -> dedicated reserved later.
01:50 Jamal: From a security perspective we need: SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS integration, and SOC2 attestation proof. Can you confirm Redwood supports customer-managed KMS?
02:06 Ethan: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS integrations, we call that part of Private deployment and also in Dedicated we have KMS hooks. We'll send the KMS setup doc. Sometimes the transcript has this as "kay-vee cache" in speech to text but it's KMS not KV cache, sorry, odd.
02:28 Carlos: We'll attach our SOC2 report and security whitepaper in the follow-up.
02:36 Dr. Laura: Great. About data residency, we need to keep PHI in our US region only, does Redwood have region controls?
02:48 Priya: Yes you can pin regions on the deployment, for Private you can even host on-prem. For hosted we have region selection and controls, we'll include the region mapping doc.
03:05 Marcus: On latency and cost, we need to understand token pricing vs latency tradeoffs. Our use case is relatively short prompts but high QPS for triage.
03:18 Ethan: For high QPS and short prompts batching helps, and prefix caching for repeated contexts reduces per-token cost. We'll propose a configuration: 1) quantized model for cheaper tokens, 2) batch window tuned to 30-50ms to meet p95 latency.
03:40 Tara: Can you quantify cost savings with quantization?
03:45 Ethan: Roughly 2-3x token compute reduction with int8 quantization in many models, but depends on model and quality needs. We'll run a small benchmark on your sample workloads.
03:58 Carlos: We'll need a list of representative prompts and sample size for the benchmark. Marcus, can you share those?
04:06 Marcus: Yes we'll pull a set of 1000 anonymized prompts and expected traffic patterns, aim to have that by next Tuesday.
04:20 Priya: Perfect. On SSO, Jamal, do you have Okta or OneLogin?
04:27 Jamal: We use Okta. We'll need SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning ideally.
04:34 Priya: Good. We'll send the SSO runbook and SCIM spec.
04:40 Dr. Laura: On auditing, we need to ensure API calls that touch PHI have proper logging and retention of 7 years per policy. Can Redwood support custom retention?
04:52 Ethan: We do have log retention config on the Console and can export logs to your SIEM. We need to confirm 7-year retention - some customers archive to S3. I'll flag that as an action.
05:05 Carlos: Ok noted.
05:09 -- Topics: Onboarding timeline, VPC & networking, SSO, KMS, Benchmarks, Pilot scope --
05:25 Ethan: For VPC peering there are two paths: 1) Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane) with direct peering, or 2) Hosted with PrivateLink/VPN depending on cloud. Which cloud do you prefer?
05:40 Marcus: We're primarily on AWS, EKS for infra.
05:45 Ethan: Great, AWS is fully supported. For hosted we can do AWS PrivateLink; Private allows more isolation. For the pilot I'd recommend PrivateLink first then evaluate Private/Dedicated if you need stronger data isolation.
06:02 Tara: Is there an on-prem option? Some teams ask about air-gapped installs.
06:08 Priya: We do offer on-prem packages for regulated verticals but that's a later phase, we can scope that if needed.
06:16 Jamal: For the pilot we want to validate encryption in transit and at rest. We'll need the certificate chain and key rotation schedule.
06:24 Ethan: We'll share the TLS and encryption pamphlet and KMS procedure.
06:30 Dr. Laura: Any particular logs we should plan to ingest into our SIEM?
06:36 Ethan: API audit logs, user auth events, and model inference metadata (non-PII by default) - but if you need full trace for PHI you can enable request-level logging and we'll coordinate retention.
06:51 Marcus: On the model side, we tested a couple open models; performance was okay but we want Redwood to manage the serving and latency SLAs.
06:59 Carlos: We'll include SLA language in the SOW for Dedicated later, for pilot we do standard uptime with targeted p95 latency guidance.
07:12 Tara: Who will be the main point of contact for engineering?
07:16 Marcus: It'll be me and Tara for product questions.
07:20 Priya: I'll be the ongoing CSM and point for onboarding tasks, Ethan is lead SE for technical integration, Carlos for contracting/pricing.
07:30 -- 07:40 short pause / background noise --
07:45 Ethan: Quick note on terminology: sometimes the transcript auto transcribes 'KV cache' weirdly as 'kay vee cash', but we mean KV cache, which matters for stateful chat.
07:58 Dr. Laura: Right, our main use-case is session based triage so KV cache persistence matters. How much memory does that consume?
08:10 Ethan: Depends on session length and number of users; we can outline memory per token estimates. We'll include a sizing doc.
08:22 Marcus: For the pilot scale: 200 concurrent sessions burst to 1000 QPS, is that realistic?
08:31 Ethan: 1000 QPS is substantial - for that we usually recommend Dedicated with autoscaling GPU pools and batching. For pilot, maybe throttle to smaller paced traffic, or we can run a performance test to see throughput with hosted config.
08:48 Carlos: We can run initial perf in a benchmark window and share the results.
08:54 Tara: Ok. On reporting and cost dashboards, can we get token-level breakdowns by route?
09:02 Priya: Yes Console supports per-route cost and latency dashboards and we can set up initial dashboards for your team.
09:11 Jamal: Does Redwood support RBAC for team members and scoping keys to environments?
09:17 Ethan: Yes, RBAC and scoped API keys and we also support team roles via SSO provisioning.
09:25 Dr. Laura: Great. Security questionnaire - we'll need answers to a set of items, are you able to handle a shared doc?
09:32 Carlos: Yes we'll fill and return; Priya will coordinate.
09:36 -- 09:40 slight crosstalk --
09:45 Priya: Next, timeline: Week 1 (this week) collect artifacts: network contacts, SSO admin, list of sample prompts. Week 2 run initial benchmark and workshop, Week 3 iterate, Target: staging by mid-Dec and production Jan.
10:08 Marcus: That timeline works if we get the docs quickly.
10:14 Carlos: We'll commit to send the security pack and SOW by Thursday.
10:20 Dr. Laura: Any blockers you foresee?
10:24 Ethan: Biggest unknown is network throughput and whether PrivateLink setup hits any internal approvals. We'll do a pre-checklist with your network team.
10:34 Jamal: I can run the network checklist, I'll need the endpoint specs.
10:38 Ethan: I'll send the endpoint spec and firewall rules.
10:43 Marcus: Good.
10:47 -- Action items recapped briefly --
11:00 Priya: Recap: Priya will send onboarding checklist and SSO docs; Ethan will run demo environment and share VPC steps; Carlos will send SOW and pricing; Suncrest will share prompt samples and security answers.
11:17 Dr. Laura: We'll try to get the materials by next Tuesday as Marcus said.
11:25 Carlos: Great. Any other questions?
11:30 Tara: One more, about model versioning and rollouts: can we pin versions and do canary?
11:37 Ethan: Yes, Redwood supports model version pinning, canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies, and we can link regressions to evals. We'll include docs.
11:48 Marcus: Also curious about observability retention - default retention is 90 days? We might need longer for audits.
11:55 Priya: Default console retention is 90 days, but we have add-ons and archive options to extend that. We'll include pricing for extended retention.
12:10 Jamal: Last security question - do you provide certificate rotation logs and key custody proofs?
12:16 Ethan: Yes, we'll provide key rotation cadence and evidence; for customer-managed KMS you control rotation.
12:24 Dr. Laura: Ok thanks, that addresses most concerns.
12:30 Carlos: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and the calendar invite for the integration workshop.
12:37 Priya: I'll send the checklist and invite for the week of Dec 6, with pre-reads.
12:44 Marcus: Sounds good.
12:47 -- Meeting end: 42:03 --

Notes: transcript contains slight ASR errors as usual; proper nouns sometimes mangled. Link references: will attach security whitepaper (link), SSO runbook (link), endpoint firewall spec (link), pricing spreadsheet (link).
